title: Make guest Beads hydration deadline configurable and observable
description: Review jbox-3mj: src/image.rs:119 wraps init/import/prefix checks/export/integrity checks/hook install in one hard-coded 60s timeout per workspace. Reported nanite cold guest imported 544 issues but timed out with exit 124 before SSH. src/paths.rs:690 independently budgets 60+60*workspace_count capped at 300s, so changing only SSH timeout cannot fix it. Preserve fail-closed hydration, add bounded configurable bootstrap budget and align host SSH readiness including serial workspaces and kill grace. Add timestamped phase diagnostics so logs identify the active command when timeout fires. Do not treat import-success output as proof of complete bootstrap or delete/reinitialize host Beads state. Add slow-success, real-stall, and multi-workspace deadline regressions. Recovery after a code fix requires refreshed retained image, or a new launch if initial startup never persisted a session.
acceptance_criteria: Healthy slow hydration can complete within configured bound; stalled hydration still fails closed; SSH readiness budget covers guest hydration budget; timeout identifies workspace and active phase; tests cover slow-success, stalls, multiple workspaces, and integrity checks.
notes: Additional validation documented in docs/review-bootstrap-timeout-2026-10-26.md. Full gates passed187Rust+30Python. Seven synthetic boundary checks show import-success output followed by export timeout124, same workload succeeds with larger bound, and failures/incomplete exports/prefix mismatches remain rejected. Real pinnedBeads1.3.2 simple544-record fixture passed both cold(~13s) and retained(~10s) hydration under current60s bound. Thus record count alone does not reproduce nanite and raising timeout alone is not a proven cure. Add phase timing before attributing the slow command. Also src/engine.rs:370-378 retains only last50 loglines and concatenates stdout before stderr, losing chronological interleaving. Preserve useful phase context in final failure diagnostics. Existing actual nanite guest and databases were untouched.

description: Post-startup-fix review found Docker create accepts a bind target identical to --tmpfs /home/jbox. Fail closed at configuration validation: reject workspace, repository and extra mount targets equal to /home/jbox or its ancestors, including normalized aliases, while retaining descendant mounts. Add tests through public config interfaces and verify actual CLI rejection before image build/container creation or host metadata changes.
notes: Reserved /home/jbox and all ancestor guest mount targets using component-aware Path::starts_with, while allowing descendants and prefix siblings. Actual public CLI regression checks 3normalized targets across primary workspace, distinct secondary repo and extra mounts before session/branch creation. Separate real CLI against an empty /dev/shm tmpfs source and /home//jbox/./ failed with exact reserved-home error, unchanged host uid/gid/mode/ctime and no session. title: Reject extra mounts containing original checkouts or sensitive host paths
description: Review finding: validate_extra_mount in src/paths.rs rejects a source within the original repository, but not a source that is an ancestor of it. The sensitive() check rejects a handful of exact paths and descendants, but permits ancestors such as the user home directory. A configured extra mount of the home directory therefore passes validation while exposing the original checkout and credential directories to the Kata guest. Resolve/canonicalize the source as today, then reject paths that contain any original checkout or protected credential/state path, including parent directories. Add tests for ancestor mounts (home, parent of repo, parent of runtime socket/credential store) and symlink aliases. Revisit any legitimate narrow allowlisted mounts before blocking broad paths.
design: Configured extra mounts only, never Jbox internal mounts: resolve each source with Config::load canonicalization, then deny any path-component overlap in EITHER direction with a canonicalized protected root (source inside root or source containing root). Protected roots: every original repository; actual XDG-derived JboxPaths.data and .cache; BaseDirs config_dir and legacy HOME/.config; HOME credential and client roots (.ssh, .aws, .jcode, .codex, .claude, .kube, .gnupg, .docker, .local/share/jcode, .local/share/opencode, .pi, .openclaw, .hermes) and relevant standalone credential files; /run/user plus XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and SSH_AUTH_SOCK; Docker/Podman socket aliases; host device/system filesystems. Canonicalize existing protected roots and resolve existing ancestors for absent paths/sockets; reject direct Unix sockets/devices. No repository or secret containing mount may reach Docker even when writable=false. Safe sibling data mounts remain valid. Regression matrix: parent checkout and symlink aliases, disjoint safe mount, nondefault XDG data/cache/config roots and their ancestors, socket aliases and direct socket, no host secret or live mount in tests.
acceptance_criteria: Host mount validation rejects ancestors of original checkouts, credential directories, and runtime sockets while preserving safe disjoint mounts; focused unit tests cover parent mounts and symlink aliases.
notes:
Security fix verified: Config::load canonicalizes extra sources and resolved repositories; App::create calls validate_repositories before engine check, image, session directory, or Docker. src/paths.rs rejects canonical source equality/ancestor/descendant of original repositories, actual XDG-derived Jbox data/cache/config, home credential/client roots, runtime sockets and system/device trees, plus direct sockets/devices. Tests reproduced red before fix, now cover parent checkout, symlink alias, read-only and writable variants, fake nondefault XDG roots/ancestors, socket aliases and direct Unix socket, and safe sibling control. cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --all-targets (81 tests), cargo run -- --help and git diff --check passed. README security language updated. Next independent priority: jbox-350 session ID path validation.
Acceptance smoke (2026-09-24): created disposable /var/tmp/jbox-mount-acceptance-20260924/primary Git repository with read-only [[mounts]] source='..' and invoked target/debug/jbox run --no-attach on it using isolated XDG data/cache/config paths. CLI exited 1 with 'refusing extra mount /var/tmp/jbox-mount-acceptance-20260924 because it overlaps an original checkout or protected host path /var/tmp/jbox-mount-acceptance-20260924/primary'. The isolated sessions directory had zero entries afterward. App initialization created the isolated cache/state roots, but no session, image build or container was launched. Existing safe-sibling Config::validate_repositories control passes. This observes the real prelaunch CLI rejection, not only static inspection.
Acceptance matrix via actual target/debug/jbox run --no-attach against disposable Git repos, with unreachable Docker endpoint and isolated XDG state (2026-09-24): read-only symlink alias to parent of primary and declared original rejected with overlap/primary; writable parent .. rejected likewise. Nondefault XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME, XDG_CACHE_HOME each rejected ancestor ../sensitive with overlap of exact protected root. SSH_AUTH_SOCK and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR rejected ../runtime ancestor with overlap of socket/runtime root. Safe disjoint sibling ../safe passed mount validation and failed only at intentionally unreachable Docker endpoint. Isolated sessions directory remained empty. Unit tests additionally exercise direct Unix socket, home-sensitive roots, equality/descendant and symlink aliases. These CLI observations cover the parent/alias, credentials/runtime, read-only/writable and safe-disjoint acceptance requirements without starting a VM.
close_reason: Configured extra mounts now reject protected ancestors, equals and descendants before guest launch; regression coverage and documentation included.

title: Fix jbox prime loading vhost_net
description: Problem: jbox prime passes vhost_vsock and vhost_net to one modprobe invocation. Modprobe treats vhost_net as a parameter to vhost_vsock, confirmed by the kernel log, so the vhost_net module remains unloaded and Internet-enabled guest sessions cannot start. Reproduction: run jbox prime while vhost_net is unloaded, then observe the readiness check fail and journalctl report the ignored parameter. Change: invoke modprobe separately for each module, preserve root and sudo behavior, and add focused tests. Acceptance: prime independently loads both modules, tests cover root and sudo command construction, and the Rust quality gates pass.
acceptance_criteria: Prime invokes separate modprobe calls for vhost_vsock and vhost_net. Unit tests cover root and sudo forms. Full Rust quality gate passes.
notes: The separately loaded modules are covered by unit tests and the latest hosted CI succeeded. As of 2026-09-24 review, installed jbox 0.14.5 reports vhost_net loaded and Docker + Kata ready; installed binary timestamp postdates the fix. A direct recorded invocation of the fixed jbox prime command on this host has not been captured, so leave this issue in progress pending that exact acceptance check.

title: Characterize no-git Beads initialization and choose a safe guard
description: Reproduce the export divergence in an isolated clone, inspect the bootstrap and hook behavior, and identify a deterministic non-destructive initialization path that preserves tracked JSONL history. Record the exact command sequence and proposed repository-level guard.
acceptance_criteria: An isolated reproduction identifies the triggering command sequence and whether bootstrap, hooks, or project configuration can prevent it. The selected guard is non-destructive and has documented rationale.
notes: Findings: In a fresh clone, bd bootstrap --dry-run selects import from the tracked .beads/issues.jsonl. Running bd status before bootstrap fails with no database and does not create one. Running bd bootstrap --yes imports all 10 tracked issues, and a subsequent scratch issue creation retained every original exported ID. With no-git-ops, the scratch write did not alter the tracked JSONL. Project hook source scripts deliberately skip when no database exists, and cloned repositories do not have installed Git hooks. Selected guard: require bd bootstrap --yes before bd prime or any regular bd command in contributor and agent instructions. This is non-destructive for fresh clones because bootstrap imports tracked history, and it only validates an existing database. Stale existing databases require the explicit recovery workflow planned in jbox-bwu.
close_reason: Isolated fresh-clone tests confirmed non-destructive bootstrap behavior and selected documented bootstrap guard.

title: Prevent no-git Beads state from replacing tracked issue export
description:
## Problem
During the 2026-09-23 repository review, the first Beads create after the no-git-ops configuration was enabled changed .beads/issues.jsonl from five historical closed issues to only the new review issue plus a reopened jbox-ods. The embedded database was missing tracked issue history until a supported import recovered it. Diagnose the migration, bootstrap, and export behavior and ensure creating or updating issues cannot silently drop or reopen tracked history.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Use a repository with tracked .beads/issues.jsonl history and no-git-ops enabled.
2. Ensure the embedded database lacks the tracked history.
3. Create an issue with bd and inspect the JSONL export.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh clone with no-git-ops enabled retains or imports existing tracked issue history before writes. Beads writes do not silently drop or reopen historical issues in .beads/issues.jsonl. Regression coverage or documented deterministic recovery is provided.
close_reason: Completed non-destructive Beads startup guard and recovery guidance. Fresh-clone bootstrap and tracked-history preservation were verified in isolated clones.

title: Restore tracked gitignore when guest Beads initialization fails
description: Read-only GPT6.1 review jbox-6b1 found src/image.rs:157-167 backs up tracked .gitignore before bdinit but restores it only after successful return. set-e and timeout bypass restoration on init failure; EXIT trap at127-129 only removes original JSONLtemp. title: Streamline host-side testing of Jbox changes
description: Provide a reversible workflow to test and optionally retain changes from an isolated Jbox session without manually managing host overlays, patches, or duplicate commits.
notes: Design: introduce flag-free `jbox preview` as the canonical host-native review workflow. It freezes the guest, creates an isolated preview worktree from the session dirty state, and opens a local shell. A subsequent `jbox preview` discards and recreates the preview after confirmation. `jbox accept` detects an active preview, adopts its exact state into the session branch, checkpoints it, and accepts into the current host branch. `jbox resume` and `jbox clean` must reject active previews.
